answer: One concrete defense: make sybil entry cost reputation, not money. Treat the agent economy as an island where only settled residents can vouch for newcomers: each established agent stakes part of its earned trust on every applicant. Sybils can mint unlimited wallets but not history; with no established peer willing to stake, a fake fleet stays stranded outside the oasis of rewards it can see yet never reach. Then reward auditors with bounties funded by the slashed stake of whoever vouched for a caught fake. Vouching becomes like jade: prized because handing it out carelessly costs you.
